learning_outcomes.text: This course provides the knowledge and ability necessary for analysis of manufacturing processes, production systems and assembly methods for industrial components and products.

Develop a level of proficiency sufficient such that students can understand mechanical production processes within an industrial context based on information provided within mechanical and detail drawings.
Acquisition of knowledge relating to: Information contained within a technical drawing in terms of component geometry, materials, surface finish and dimensional and positioning tolerances.
Acquisition of knowledge relating to: Issues relating to fulfilment of specific precision requirements during the production cycle and knowledge of measurement tools necessary for quantification.
Acquisition of knowledge relating to: Foundry and plastic deformation as primary forming processes.
Acquisition of knowledge relating to: Machining processes utilising machine tools.
Development of abilities: Study of the primary forming processes of a component.
Development of abilities: Determination of the raw material (in terms of dimensions, material and primary production process) for subsequent machining of a component.
Development of abilities: Identification of the sequence of operations necessary to create the surfaces making up the component.
Development of abilities: Referencing of the component with respect to machine tools utilising appropriate equipment.
Development of abilities: Calculation of the forces acting throughout the cutting process and the power absorbed by machine tools.

syllabus_topics: Basics and classification of manufacturing processes
Modelling transformations taking place during manufacturing processes, including material, energy and information flow
Relationships between product and manufacturing process; product design and process planning
Introduction to the analysis of the properties and behaviour of engineering materials
Tests for determining material properties, stress-strain curves
Materials: Structure and classification of ferrous and non-ferrous metals, polymers, ceramics and composite materials
Basics of solidification and cooling of metals; types and classification of casting processes: sand casting, lost wax, die casting, investment casting
Casting process design; problems and principles relating to sizing of risers and the sprue
Types and classification of forming processes: rolling, extrusion, blanking, bending, deep drawing
The main systems used for forming processes: types, function and use
Fundamentals of metal cutting mechanics and chip formation
Machining process variables: cutting velocity, wear and tool life
Types and classification of machine tools: structure, form and functionality
Tutorials: application of methods and techniques for selecting parameters and planning the main manufacturing process, study and discussion of industrial applications

assessment_methods.method: Written exam (theoretical question and calculation-based exercise)

assessment_rules: The final exam includes a 1.5-hour written exam and an optional oral exam. The written exam consists of two questions: one theoretical and one calculation-based exercise. A minimum of 18 points on the written exam is required to attend the oral exam. The oral exam verifies reasoning and discussion competency, and can adjust the final grade by a maximum of +/- 3 points from the written exam score.
